saw_lines: Wide foot buyers choose by width and comfort, not brand, and they reorder only after a pair stops hurting.
So the sale is decided in the first line, where a shopper checks whether the shoe fits their foot.
Your site shows review counts from 178 to 999, yet none of your 30 ads carries one. Put 999 reviews on the creative and open two ads with a foot doctor quote.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 25 Nov 2026
points: Your site shows review counts from 178 to 999, yet none of your 30 ads carries one. Shoppers buying wide shoes need that proof before the click. Put 999 reviews on the creative and open two ads with a foot doctor quote.

4 of 29 ads are creator style posts, with codes, #ad tags or @mentions, run as brand ads. Buyers read that as a sponsored pitch and scroll past. Whitelist those posts from the creator account, then cut three variations of each post.

18 different openings run across 29 copy ads, and the biggest leads only 4. Shoppers see a new story every scroll, so none sticks. Keep the uncomfortable shoes opener and the wide feet question, then build the batch from those two.

29 of your ads have run 60+ days, and the oldest has run since November 2025. Those are proven winners, so copy the wide feet angle. Make three variations of the Up To 6E video, keeping the 6E width line up front.

ads_1: Review quote creative with the 6E width line, built from the oldest winner
soc_1: Brand social strategy across Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, TikTok, Twitter and YouTube
